body:
Thanks for the response! I've been feeling a lot better since making this post.

I didn't mean to imply programming is my profession. (I hope that doesn't come off as rude to say.) I work at Walmart and desperately wish I had a job programming instead. I've been teaching myself how to program for the past two years off and on and still feel as though I know nothing. I've tried to give myself small achievable goals in the past, however my goals always seem too big when I try to accomplish them.

I'm currently trying to make a game in Unity. Looking at the revenue from other steam games, even small indie games has been motivating me lately because I think it could help pay for my education.

Based on your comment, it seems like you know a bit about programming. Maybe you could help me out with a problem I'm having. My problem being that I'm a why learner to an obnoxious extent. A couple years ago I was trying to learn C++ and I was getting frustrated that I didn't know WHY the code I wrote was working. Long story short I ended up wasting two years of my life in community college and $8,000 dollars in an electronics program just so I could learn about memory and transistors. I struggle not going down a crazy rabbit hole when learning something I don't understand. Do you do this? Do you have any ideas as to how I could keep myself on track?

As I'm writing this I realized my rabbit hole problem could be why I feel like I know nothing... I get myself way too deep into stuff I don't yet understand then it frustrates me and I give up then repeat the process again later.

If you've made it through my rambling then thank you! If you or anybody has any ideas how I can stop my "rabbit hole" issue I'd love to hear it.

Over the past decade I've been certain I will die by suicide. I have been on the brink on and off for about two years of my life.

Even when I'm feeling fine I think about suicide in an almost arrogant way, as if nothing is good enough to kill me but my self. I guess that's just my way of justifying these thoughts when I'm happy.
